SI-3_author_journal_year.answer: Floris et al., Nature Mental Health, 2025

SI-4_title.answer: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative models were trained using Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) with PCNtoolkit package (version 0.26). A B-spline basis expansion of the covariate vector was used to model non-linear effects of age. Models were derived under 10-fold cross-validation.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: normative models were trained using Bayesian linear regression; As in prior work, normative models were trained across all individuals using Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) using PCNtoolkit package (version 0.26)
NM2-1_modeling_methods.location: Floris2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling; 44220_2024_349_MOESM1_ESM.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Normative Modeling

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: Four imaging modalities were used: (1) Structural MRI: voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-derived voxel-wise gray matter (GM) volumes; (2) Resting-state fMRI: seed-based correlation between the FFA and remaining FFG voxels (FFA connectivity); (3) Task-fMRI: T-contrast maps reflecting sensitivity to faces (faces vs. shapes condition from Hariri paradigm); (4) EEG: principal component of source-reconstructed activation across cortical FFG parcels.
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: the features for subsequent normative modeling were as follows (1) structure: voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-derived, voxel-wise GM volumes, (2) rs-fMRI: seed-based correlation between the FFA and the remaining FFG, (3) task-fMRI: T-contrast maps reflecting sensitivity to faces and (4) EEG: the principal component of source-reconstructed activation obtained across different cortical FFG parcels.

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age (with B-spline basis expansion for non-linear effects), sex, and scanning site were used as covariates in the normative models. The B-spline basis expansion captures higher-order age effects beyond linear terms.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we trained normative models using Bayesian linear regression for each brain imaging modality within the right and left FFG region of interest (ROI) independently using age, sex and scanning site as covariates. A B-spline basis expansion of the covariate vector was used to model nonlinear effects of age.
